name: sdrmm
why: A client-server software-defined radio system, a neat architectural idea for listening to the airwaves with real hardware.

brief.what_it_is: SDR-- (the brew formula calls it sdrmm) is a software-defined radio application for listening, decoding, and recording. You plug in a radio (the README's first example is an RTL-SDR dongle) and wire up nodes on a canvas: a Device node for the radio, channel nodes such as WFM, and displays and outputs such as a Speaker. It can run as a desktop app with a local SDR, or as a server near the antenna that you reach from a browser; both use the same receiver engine and interface. Outputs include audio, decoded messages, maps, recordings, and network IQ, and a phone remote is also offered. The brew formula's desc calls it a modular, client-server software-defined radio, which matches the server-plus-browser design the README describes.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a single application for listening, decoding, and recording radio signals, with a layout that puts connections in a Patch view and everyday controls in a Rack view. It also positions the server as something you can put near an antenna and reach remotely, rather than a desktop-only tool.
brief.how_it_works: Radios, channels, and displays are nodes you connect with wires in the Patch view; for example, Device iq is wired to WFM iq, and WFM audio to the Speaker. Nodes you use often can be pinned to the Rack view with the p key. The desktop app and the server share one receiver engine, so the browser interface and the local app behave the same. The README says Automation is available through REST, WebSocket, and MCP APIs.

brief.install_notes: The README points to GitHub Releases for a desktop installer or portable server, and to the install guide at sdrmm.com/docs covering macOS, Windows, Linux, Homebrew, APT, DNF, Nix, and Docker (I did not open that guide). The README's first-run steps: plug in the RTL-SDR, pick it on the Device node, set the rate to 2.4 MS/s, add a WFM channel set to a local FM station, wire Device iq to WFM iq and WFM audio to the Speaker, then start the Speaker. Release notes mention an APT and DNF repository at downloads.sdrmm.com that has to be re-added with commands from the install guide. Other hardware (Airspy, AntSDR, FUNcube Dongle, Aaronia, KrakenRF) is listed as supported or tested; the release notes also mention ESP32 boards running ESP-SDR firmware, and AntSDR streaming over Ethernet.
brief.standout: It combines a visual patch-and-rack signal graph with a very broad decoder catalogue (aircraft, ships, pagers, digital voice, weather satellites, DAB, DVB, and more) in one app. It also ships with automation hooks (REST, WebSocket, MCP) and a phone remote, which is unusual for a radio tool.
brief.status: Maintained. The releases page shows v2.3.0 marked Latest, with assets timestamped 2026-10-20, and a nightly pre-release built from main on the same date. The earlier releases run back through v1.7.0 with regular feature and fix notes.
brief.caveats: The README does not list platform requirements, build dependencies, or the license beyond AGPL-3.0-or-later and a commercial license offer. The repo name is Newspicel/sdrminusminus, while the releases and Docker image live under Newspicel/sdrmm, so the naming is split across repos and the brew name (sdrmm) differs from the app name (SDR--). The v2.3.0 release notes flag breaking changes to the REST API. I did not read the sdrmm.com docs, so hardware support details come from the README and release notes only. The releases page output was truncated.
